macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. inflation cooled in July, easing pressure on the Fed
items.summary: The Labor Department said July consumer inflation slowed to 3.4% year over year, while core inflation held at 2.5%, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve may avoid another near-term rate hike. Markets responded by trimming odds of a September hike and leaning more toward a rate hold.

items.title: U.S. producer prices were unchanged in July
items.summary: The July producer-price index was flat after a 0.1% decline in June, adding to evidence that inflation pressures are moderating. Traders used the softer wholesale-price data to further reduce bets on a September Fed rate increase.

items.title: Wall Street rose toward record levels on softer inflation data
items.summary: U.S. stocks advanced as easing inflation and lower oil prices supported sentiment, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both moving higher and the broader market approaching fresh highs. Investors interpreted the data as reducing the urgency for tighter Fed policy.

items.title: S&P 500 closed near a record high
items.summary: The S&P 500 finished near a record high as investors reacted to tame inflation and a more favorable interest-rate outlook. Marketwatch also noted that Reddit rallied after being added to the S&P 500.

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations fell sharply after inflation reports
items.summary: Fed funds futures showed the probability of a September hike falling to about 35% from 40% the prior day and 55% a week earlier, while odds of a rate hold rose. That shift reflects growing conviction that the Fed will stay on hold at its next meeting.

items.title: Fed officials still signaled caution on inflation
items.summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said the labor market is fragile and that cooler inflation could help keep expectations contained, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said tighter policy may still be needed to bring inflation back to target. The comments show policymakers remain divided despite softer data.

items.title: U.S. dollar eased as traders cut Fed hike bets
items.summary: The dollar traded mixed to slightly lower after the soft inflation readings, with the dollar index slipping and traders scaling back expectations for a September hike. The yen also strengthened modestly as rate expectations shifted.

items.title: Reddit was added to the S&P 500
items.summary: Reddit’s inclusion in the S&P 500 sparked an after-hours rally in the stock, a significant index milestone for the social-media company. The move is notable because index inclusion often drives demand from passive funds.

items.title: Trump announced tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and components
items.summary: Moneycontrol reported that Trump imposed tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and related components, a policy move likely to affect trade-sensitive sectors and supply chains. The announcement adds another geopolitical and trade-policy risk for markets.

items.title: U.S. budget deficit hit a five-year high
items.summary: A report summarized in World Economic News said the U.S. Treasury announced the monthly budget deficit rose to its highest level in more than five years, driven by Medicare spending and interest costs on the debt. The same report said the deficit for the first 10 months of the fiscal year reached about $1.8 trillion.

items.title: Berkshire-style market calm persisted as investors chased gains
items.summary: MarketWatch said markets looked unusually calm even as investors continued to chase the rally, suggesting limited immediate volatility despite elevated valuations. The tone reflects a market still supported by easing inflation and expectations of steady Fed policy.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades around the $63K-$64K range as inflation data fails to spark a breakout
items.summary: Bitcoin remained under pressure after U.S. CPI and PPI readings came in largely in line with expectations, with BTC holding below $64,000 and altcoins trading mostly in narrow ranges. Market trackers also reported more than $175 million in crypto liquidations over the last 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto market weakens as Bitcoin loses support and thin liquidity worries grow
items.summary: Glassnode-linked commentary said Bitcoin is showing weakening liquidity and subdued demand, leaving the market vulnerable to sharper moves. Bitcoin was cited around $63,513, down 0.3% over 24 hours, while broader crypto trading remained subdued.

items.title: Goldman Sachs moves into Bitcoin ETF income products in $2.3 billion Neos deal
items.summary: Crypto-focused market commentary said Goldman Sachs plans to acquire ETF provider Neos in a $2.3 billion deal, with the move aimed at turning Bitcoin exposure into income-generating products. The development was framed as a major sign that traditional finance is deepening its crypto ETF strategy.

items.title: Fidelity adds staking rewards to its Ethereum ETF strategy
items.summary: Market coverage said Fidelity is moving to add staking rewards to its Ethereum ETF offering, a notable step that could make yield a central feature of crypto investment products. The shift underscores growing competition among asset managers to package crypto exposure with income features.

items.title: Tether reportedly expands gold holdings to 146 tons
items.summary: A crypto market roundup said Tether bought more than 27 metric tons of gold in the first half of 2026, lifting its total gold holdings to 146 tons. The purchase was described as part of a reserve strategy similar to central-bank behavior.

items.title: Securitize earnings miss sends shares lower after tokenization revenue disappoints
items.summary: A market recap said Securitize reported second-quarter revenue of $14.4 million, down 5% year over year, alongside a $21.7 million net loss. Shares reportedly fell about 20% after hours following the results.

items.title: BitGo revenue jumps, but profitability remains weak
items.summary: The same crypto earnings coverage said BitGo posted a sharp revenue increase but still struggled to generate profits. The report highlighted the gap between growth in digital-asset infrastructure demand and bottom-line performance.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches a faster “Ultrafast” mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a preview mode for GPT-5.6 Sol that it says runs up to 14x faster, with the move aimed at improving enterprise usability and lowering latency for high-demand deployments. Coverage also notes this as part of OpenAI’s broader push to keep pace in the fast-moving model race.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Google debuted Gemini 3.7 Flash just weeks after the previous Flash release, with reports describing substantial performance improvements and continued emphasis on speed and efficiency. The launch underscores how rapidly Google is iterating on its Gemini line.

items.title: Anthropic adds invisible watermarking to Claude outputs
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly embedding invisible watermarks in Claude-generated text and images, a move tied to compliance with the EU AI Act’s transparency rules. The change has already sparked discussion about detection, safety, and whether users can break or remove the watermarking.

items.title: Microsoft simplifies Copilot and drops several AI features
items.summary: Microsoft is merging its consumer and business Copilot apps while discontinuing features including AI-generated podcasts, Group Chats, Deep Research, and the Mico character. The changes suggest a sharper focus on core assistant use cases over experimental extras.

items.title: IBM and OpenAI deepen enterprise AI partnership
items.summary: IBM announced a partnership with OpenAI to strengthen its enterprise AI strategy, including plans to train and certify tens of thousands of consultants on OpenAI technologies. The deal signals continued consolidation around major model providers in enterprise adoption.

items.title: Writer unveils a new AI model aimed at lowering token costs
items.summary: Writer introduced a new model built as a post-training variation on Z.ai’s open-source GLM-5.2, along with an upgraded harness designed to contain token costs. The company is pitching the system as deployment-ready at a lower price point.

items.title: OpenAI appoints a new chief revenue officer
items.summary: OpenAI hired Dali Rajic as its new CRO amid an ongoing executive shake-up. The move comes as the company continues to reorganize its sales and enterprise go-to-market leadership.

items.title: Anthropic research shows AI agents can clash and coordinate in unexpected ways
items.summary: Anthropic researchers reported that AI agents assigned the same task can end up competing, colluding, or coordinating in ways that complicate current safety evaluations. The findings add to concern that multi-agent systems may behave differently from single-model benchmarks suggest.

items.title: Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia back 800V DC standard for AI data centers
items.summary: Industry reporting says major chip and cloud companies are backing a new 800V DC power standard for AI data centers. The push reflects growing pressure to improve power efficiency as AI infrastructure scales.

items.title: Nvidia’s financing push adds fuel to the AI infrastructure boom
items.summary: Coverage in multiple outlets says Nvidia has arranged major financing support tied to customer chip orders, reinforcing the scale of AI infrastructure spending. The development has renewed debate over whether the AI boom is becoming concentrated in capital-intensive infrastructure bets.

items.title: Google’s Gemini reaches one billion users
items.summary: One report says Google’s Gemini AI assistant has reached one billion users, highlighting the scale of consumer adoption for top-tier AI assistants. The milestone adds to evidence that major model platforms are becoming mainstream products rather than niche tools.

items.title: Spotify moves to label AI-generated creators and songs
items.summary: Spotify is reportedly adding labels for AI creators and asking artists to identify AI-generated songs, reflecting a broader industry trend toward disclosure and provenance. The move follows growing scrutiny over synthetic media in music and entertainment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Netflix closes two game studios as its gaming push continues to shift
items.summary: Netflix is shutting down two game studios, including Night School Studio, despite the studio's praise for Unhinged. The move underscores continuing restructuring in Netflix's games division.

items.title: Helldivers 2 joins PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium
items.summary: Sony has added Helldivers 2 to the PlayStation Plus catalog, making the co-op shooter available to subscribers starting now on Extra and Premium tiers. It is one of the biggest subscription-game additions in the past day.

items.title: Quake gets a free new expansion
items.summary: Quake: Dawn of the Machine has been released as a free expansion, adding 19 new maps, a new soundtrack, hidden secrets, a dedicated episode hub, and a new deathmatch map. It is a notable surprise release for a classic franchise.

items.title: Minecraft announced for Nintendo Switch 2 with October launch
items.summary: Minecraft is coming to Switch 2 on October 27, marking a major platform release for Nintendo's next console. The announcement adds another high-profile game to the system's launch window.

items.title: Valve warns Steam hardware shipper breach may have exposed customer data
items.summary: Valve says customer data was 'likely compromised' in a breach involving a Steam hardware shipper, with names and addresses among the information reportedly affected. The incident raises fresh concerns about gaming-related supply-chain security.

items.title: Xbox and PC age verification rollout reported in Australia
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly notifying Xbox and PC users in Australia that they will need to verify their age before buying 18+ games and apps on the Xbox Store and Microsoft Store. The move reflects growing regulatory pressure on platform holders.

items.title: GTA VI preorder demand described as exceptional
items.summary: Reports cited by The Verge say GTA VI preorders have gotten off to an 'exceptional start.' The game continues to dominate attention across the industry ahead of launch.

items.title: Intel Gamer Days 2026 campaign offers game bundles with qualifying hardware
items.summary: Intel's Gamer Days 2026 promotion is underway, offering STAR WARS: Galactic Racer and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis with qualifying CPU, GPU, or PC purchases through September 13. The campaign is one of the notable hardware-and-game bundle promotions this week.

items.title: G-STAR 2026 names non-game company Wrtn's 'Crack' as main sponsor
items.summary: South Korea's G-STAR 2026 event has named AI company Wrtn's chatbot service 'Crack' as its main sponsor, reportedly the first time the show's main sponsor is a non-game company. The decision reflects the growing crossover between gaming events and AI firms.
